title: Nasruddin Tale 167: The Walnut and the Pumpkin
summary: Nasruddin rested beneath the shade of an enormous walnut tree beside a patch of giant pumpkins....
full_text:
Nasruddin rested beneath the shade of an enormous walnut tree beside a patch of giant pumpkins.

He pondered: "How strange is creation! Heavy pumpkins weighing twenty pounds grow on frail, crawling vines on the ground; while tiny walnuts grow on majestic, towering branches! Surely I could have arranged nature with far greater wisdom!"

Just then, a sudden breeze shook the boughs, and a heavy walnut fell straight from the high branch, striking Nasruddin squarely on the forehead!

Nasruddin rubbed his bruised brow, prostrated himself on the grass, and prayed: "Forgive my arrogant meddling, O Creator! For if giant twenty-pound pumpkins grew on high branches, my head would have been smashed to pieces this day!"
moral: Questioning divine creation often results in a walnut falling on your head.
